extracted.intended_audience: Variety readers, entertainment industry professionals and general TV/comedy audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Insights and informal guidelines for a late-night satirical show host about handling controversy, crafting jokes, audience-building, and adapting material across platforms and social norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid intentionally offensive material
rubrics_metrics.description: “I don’t strive to be offensive… That’s not who I am as a person. That’s not who I am as a performer.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not set out to offend as a goal; recognize that intent matters but that you cannot fully control what people find offensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: contextualize jokes and rely on audience understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: His fans around the world understand the context of his jokes, plus his unique sarcasm and humor, which he hopes his Comedy Central viewers will soon understand and learn to appreciate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context and a consistent comedic voice so audiences can interpret sarcasm and intent; helping the audience 'know' you reduces misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: know and build your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: “Getting to know my audience, getting my audience to know me.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a reciprocal relationship with viewers over time; audience familiarity enables riskier or more nuanced material to land.

rubrics_metrics.name: use satire to critique media and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: He will not shy away from making jokes about the media’s conflicting coverage when he starts on 'The Daily Show.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ comedic critique of media and institutions as a core function of the role, but be prepared for attention and pushback when doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: anticipate scrutiny and backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: He expected some sort of backlash when he was announced as Jon Stewart’s replacement — he just didn’t know what the media would choose to attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect heightened scrutiny when stepping into an established role; plan responses and accept that controversy is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: use controversy to prompt a broader conversation about comedy’s role
rubrics_metrics.description: “You saw the change in the conversation go from ‘Is this guy offensive?’ to ‘What is comedy and what is this role in our society?’ I think that’s a great conversation that came from it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than only defending specific jokes, reframe controversy to address larger questions about comedy, context, and social function.

rubrics_metrics.name: adapt to evolving social norms and platform cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Twitter has changed… It was a place where everybody was making jokes. Over time that changed, and I changed with it. In society, we changed and that’s progress, in my book.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update material and behavior as platforms and societal norms evolve; what was acceptable in one era or medium may not be later.

rubrics_metrics.name: leverage your unique perspective and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: “I am a 31-year-old half-black, half-white South African… Jon would comment on it from a very different place than I would because I’m more of an outsider to that world than he is.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal background and vantage point as a source of distinct angles and insights in satire and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: prioritize being extremely funny while expanding what audiences laugh at
rubrics_metrics.description: “My job at first is to be extremely funny, but what I find funny will hopefully deal with things that we would not initially laugh at.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim first for strong comedic effect, while using comedy to broaden audience tolerance for challenging topics over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: choose appropriate medium and format for material
rubrics_metrics.description: “Luckily, Comedy Central hasn’t limited me to 140 characters on the show,”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that different platforms (tweet-sized vs. long-form TV) enable different types of jokes; prefer formats that allow necessary nuance and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid immediate defensive engagement; reframe response strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Noah steered away from responding directly to the content of his tweets… he noted a shift in conversation toward larger questions about comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When controversy arises, consider steering the conversation away from point-by-point defense and toward broader, constructive dialogue.
